name: Burkina Faso
tagline: The best cinema and the best masks in West Africa
summary: FESPACO is the largest film festival on the continent, the Sindou peaks are a forest of eroded sandstone, and the mask traditions of the west are among the strongest anywhere.
when: November to February. Check advice — much of the country is affected by the wider Sahel situation.

entries.caption: The Sindou Peaks
entries.description: A ridge of sandstone eroded into fins and needles, near Banfora in the southwest.
entries.subject: the eroded sandstone fins and needles of the Sindou peaks

entries.caption: The Southwest
entries.description: Cascades, sugarcane and the Karfiguela falls where the land drops off the plateau.
entries.subject: the Karfiguela cascades falling over rock ledges near Banfora

entries.caption: Hippos at Tengrela
entries.description: A lake outside Banfora with a resident hippo pod, worked by fishermen in pirogues.
entries.subject: hippos surfacing in Lake Tengrela with a pirogue nearby

entries.caption: Nazinga and Arli
entries.description: Nazinga has one of the densest elephant populations in West Africa and you can walk in it.
entries.subject: elephants at a waterhole in Nazinga ranch

entries.caption: Tenakourou
entries.description: 747 metres in the southwest, and the highest ground in a country that is mostly plateau.
entries.subject: the sandstone escarpment of the southwest rising above farmland

entries.caption: Karfiguela
entries.description: Water off the plateau in a series of ledges, swimmable at the bottom.
entries.subject: people swimming below the Karfiguela waterfall

entries.caption: The Black and White Volta
entries.description: Two of the three Voltas rise here and run south into Ghana.
entries.subject: the Black Volta river running between wooded banks

entries.caption: Lakeshore, Not Coast
entries.description: Landlocked. Tengrela and the Bagre reservoir are where people swim and fish.
entries.subject: a fishing pirogue on Lake Tengrela at dusk

entries.caption: Gallery Forest at Banfora
entries.description: The dome-shaped Sindou woodland, and the fields of sugarcane below the cliffs.
entries.subject: gallery forest along a stream below the Banfora escarpment

entries.caption: Cycling the Southwest
entries.description: Burkina is a cycling nation. The Tour du Faso runs every year and the roads are flat.
entries.subject: cyclists on a red laterite road through savanna

entries.caption: Sixty Languages, One Cinema
entries.description: FESPACO in Ouagadougou every two years, and a film industry that punches far above its size.
entries.subject: a crowd outside a cinema at FESPACO in Ouagadougou

entries.caption: Mossi, Bobo, Lobi, Fulani
entries.description: The Mossi kingdoms in the centre, the Bobo and Lobi in the west, the Fulani across the north.
entries.subject: a Lobi compound with mud walls and a granary

entries.caption: To and Riz Gras
entries.description: To — millet paste with sauce — and riz gras cooked in tomato and oil.
entries.subject: a bowl of to with green sauce beside a plate of riz gras

entries.caption: FESPACO and FESTIMA
entries.description: The film festival in Ouagadougou, and the mask festival at Dedougou every other year.
entries.subject: masked dancers performing at the FESTIMA mask festival

entries.caption: Bronze and Masks
entries.description: Lost-wax bronze in Ouagadougou, and the plank masks of the Bwa and Nuna.
entries.subject: a tall painted Bwa plank mask with geometric patterns

entries.caption: The Ruins of Loropeni
entries.description: Stone walls six metres high, a thousand years old, from the trans-Saharan gold trade.
entries.subject: the high laterite stone walls of the Loropeni ruins

entries.caption: Loropeni, and the Living Rest
entries.description: One World Heritage site in stone, and a mask tradition that never became a museum.
entries.subject: a village mask performance with drummers and a crowd

entries.caption: Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso
entries.description: A capital that fills for FESPACO, and a second city with the country's best music.
entries.subject: the mud-brick Grande Mosquee of Bobo-Dioulasso

entries.caption: Sudanese Mud and Sukhala
entries.description: The Bobo-Dioulasso mosque in Sudanese style, and painted Kassena compounds at Tiebele.
entries.subject: the painted geometric walls of a Kassena compound at Tiebele

entries.caption: The Maquis at Night
entries.description: Open-air bars with grilled chicken and dolo, and a band more often than not.
entries.subject: an open-air maquis at night with grilled food and a band

entries.caption: Elephants You Can Walk To
entries.description: Nazinga allows walking safaris, which makes it unusually good for older children.
entries.subject: a family walking with a guide towards elephants at Nazinga

entries.caption: The Sindou Ridge
entries.description: Scrambling routes through the fins, best in the last two hours of light.
entries.subject: a walker among the sandstone fins of Sindou at sunset

entries.caption: Modest
entries.description: Good hotels in Ouagadougou and Bobo, and a lodge or two near Banfora.
entries.subject: a garden courtyard hotel in Bobo-Dioulasso

entries.caption: Nazinga
entries.description: A community-run ranch since 1979, and one of the earliest of its kind in the region.
entries.subject: a ranger and visitors watching elephants from a hide at Nazinga

entries.caption: Masks in Motion
entries.description: FESTIMA, where the masks are danced rather than displayed and the dust is part of it.
entries.subject: a masked dancer spinning in dust at a mask festival

entries.caption: Tiebele
entries.description: Kassena compounds painted in black, white and ochre geometry by the women of the household.
entries.subject: women painting geometric patterns on a Kassena wall at Tiebele

entries.caption: Why Burkina Faso
entries.description: The masks, the music and the cinema, in a country that has never traded on scenery.
entries.subject: a crowd watching a masked performance in a village square
